question: Will the 2026 World Series require a Game 6?

calls.reasoning: Base rate: in 100 World Series since 1923, 61% went 6+ games (18 sweeps, 21 five-game, 23 six-game, 38 seven-game). Brewers are about -170 series favorites, roughly 0.56 per game; independent games at that rate give about 61% to reach Game 6, so the favorite gap barely lowers it. Recent era (2015-2025) went 7/11 to Game 6. Human markets: no Game-6 contract found; Manifold Game-7 markets at 0.23 (vol 388) and 0.29 (vol 22) are near-miss evidence implying somewhat shorter series than history. Opponent (Rays lead ALCS 3-2) is undetermined but changes little.

- Brewers: 103-59, swept both NL rounds including the Dodgers in the NLCS; about -170 to win the title (Fox Sports/SI, mid-Oct 2026); 8+ day layoff before the WS. Misiorowski's whiff rate fell in the playoffs; both AL teams rank in the top five for lowest strikeout rate (SI, Oct 18).

calls.reasoning: Base rate: roughly 58% of best-of-seven World Series have gone 6+ games; a 50/50 per-game model gives 62.5%. The Brewers are about 64% favorites to win the title (Polymarket via Covers), which implies about 58% per game and a model value of about 59% for 6+ games. A comparable NLCS Over 5.5 line at -175 implies about 60% after vig. The Manifold Game-7 markets at 0.23-0.29 are consistent with a high-50s Game 6 chance. Arguments for fewer games: the Brewers' dominance (two straight sweeps), and the AL winner playing on short rest after a long ALCS. Arguments for more: the Brewers' rust after an 8-day layoff, and playoff baseball's high variance. I found no market on this exact question.

calls.reasoning: Base rate: 14 of 26 World Series from 2000-2025 (54%) reached Game 6. The all-time best-of-seven rate is roughly 56% from memory, not checked this run. Sportsbooks price the Brewers at about 65% to win the series (-170), which implies a per-game win chance of about 0.57-0.58. An independent-games model at that rate gives about 59% for a Game 6, but real series end in 4-5 games more often than that model predicts, so I shade toward the empirical rate. Manifold Game 7 markets (0.23 and 0.29, both thin) are close to the model's ~29% for a Game 7. They are a near-miss contract, so they count as weak evidence only. No market on Game 6 itself was found. The AL opponent is still undecided (ALCS was 2-2 as of the latest report found).

calls.reconciliation: Disputed: (1) the historical base rate (61% since 1923, ~58% since 1905, 54% for 2000-2025). All three are real counts over different windows. Run 3's year list checks out at 14 of 26; the all-time figures roughly match my recollection (~57-58%) but could not be verified without web access. I used the long-run figure of about 57%. (2) The ALCS state (3-2 vs 2-2) is just reports from different dates, and the opponent barely changes per-game odds. (3) Shading below the model's ~60% is a judgment call; real series have historically ended short more often than the model says, and the Brewers are strong, so I land at 0.57.
